street.description: Hyper-casual American — TikTok/Twitter native, heavy slang, profanity-adjacent.

casual_social.description: Default for US B2C social. Friendly, contraction-heavy, conversational.

professional_casual.description: LinkedIn US — confident, direct, light wit. Founder-led brand voice.

corporate_formal.description: Press releases, regulated industries, B2B legal-adjacent communication.

grammar_quirks: Heavy use of contractions (don't, won't, can't, I'm)
Sentence-initial 'And/But/So' is natural in casual register
Singular 'they' is standard in 2025-26 American English

code_switching_patterns.spanish_in_english: Spanglish in Latino US contexts — see mexican_spanish pack for cross-pollination.
rules: Avoid forced AAVE-style slang (slay, periodt, no cap) in mainstream brand voice unless audience is genuinely Black-focused — see Core Law 3.
Gen Z slang has fast half-life — verify freshness for any term older than 18 months.

do_not_use: Forced AAVE without Black-audience context (Core Law 3)
British markers (innit, peng, bare, mate) in US copy

example_translations.english: This product is amazing, you have to try it.
example_translations.correct_native_casual: Honestly, you have to try this — I'm obsessed.
example_translations.correct_native_genz: Ok this is actually unreal, you NEED to try it.
example_translations.note: Native US copy uses casual hedges ('honestly', 'ok') and intensifiers naturally.
